newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares recoup, end below day's peak.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares recoup, end below day's peak.

text.p: Hungarian shares regained almost half of Monday's losses on Tuesday as the market benefited from positive external factors, namely a stronger dollar and a firmer Dow Jones, market participants said.
The BUX index finished at 7,648.55 points, up 96.55 points or 1.28 percent, below the day's peak.
"Most of the market strengthened, but I doubt this would be a long-lasting trend," said Krisztina Marot of Rabobank Investment. "The trend will depend on the U.S. market."
The trader added that the market settled at a lower level after an early rally with the BUX peaking at 7,710.79 points.
Analysts added that the Budapest bourse's short-term outlook remains unclear and the market will move in line with Wall Street and the dollar.
Both are important driving factors for the Budapest bourse because of foreigners' high participation on the market.

"The market is uncertain in the short-term, with the impact of external factors, such as Dow Jones, strengthening," said Peter Bozso, analyst at OTP Securities. "I expect a (clear) trend to materialise within a month."
The analyst said he expected investors to become more selective and buy shares based on their fundamentals rather than recently when they bought almost all stocks.
On Tuesday pharmaceuticals Egis finished at 10,000 forints, down 250, after Nomura Equity Research said it maintained its 'sell' recommendation on the issue.
Machinery Mezogep on which Bank Austria Investment maintained its 'accumulate' rating, rose to a new high of 4,545 forints before ending at 4,470, up 70.
The day's most actively traded paper, oil company MOL edged up 15 forints to end at 4,405.
